messages:
Sam: quick heads-up — I ran a focused microbench on a fused-attn path that applies qkv packing + bias/rope fusion + epilogue fusion. results look promising but there are some odd regressions with paged KV enabled.
Maria: awesome, drop numbers? :eyes:
Sam: baseline (no fusion, CUDA kernels from stable runtime): 7B/model, seq=1024, b=8 -> forward token time ~3.4ms, mem BW ~420GB/s.
Sam: with qkv packing + bias/rope fused + epilogue fused (single kernel): token time ~2.1ms, mem BW ~610GB/s, p50 down ~38%. p99 improved but not as much when KV paged is on.
Junaid: can you paste the exact bench command and env?
Sam: sure —
Sam: ```bash
./bench/attn_bench.sh --model redwood-7b --seq 1024 --batch 8 --iters 300 --enable-fuse qkv,bias,rope,epilogue --kv-mode paged
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
```
Olga: any profiler traces? nsys / cupti?
Sam: attached summary from nsys: main kernel reduced SM utilization variance, but when paged-KV is active we see a secondary kernel (kv-page-service) that stalls L2 and increases lat tail. flamegraph attached in thread (summary): page-service spikes align with p99 spikes.
Sam: nvprof shows L2 replay rising 3x during page faults (small fragmented KVs).
Maria: hmm — is page-service doing memcpy + atomic ops? sounds like L2 thrash.
Junaid: a few ideas: 1) qkv pack reduces read footprint but epilogue fusion increases register pressure (might limit warps). 2) paged KV's scatter/gather could cause uncoalesced loads when entries are small — L2 thrash. 3) bias/rope fusion probably ok for rotary-only models but we should gate it per-arch.
Olga: agree on gating. We saw regresses on 4k+ seq earlier when epilogue blew up regs. Any occupancy numbers?
Sam: occupancy: fused kernel occupancy ~56% vs baseline 72% (regression due to extra accumulators in epilogue), but effective latency still lower for most traffic. The problem is when paged-KV triggers many small requests: occupancy dips and L2 miss rate spikes.
Maria: can we try a hybrid heuristic: use epilogue fusion only when batch*seq >= threshold AND avg-kv-segment-size >= X? fallback to two-kernel path otherwise.
Junaid: yes — suggest thresholds: min_seq >= 128 OR batch >= 4, and avg_kv_chunk >= 512 bytes. Also add runtime check for L2-replay counter: if it climbs 50% over baseline, switch to unfused epilogue for that request.
Sam: implemented a quick runtime switch in branch 'perf/hybrid-epilogue-heur' — microbench shows p50 stable and p99 tails cut by ~20% vs full-fused with paged-KV.
Olga: can you share the quick patch? would like to run the canary on dedicated infra.
Sam: patch snippet:```cpp
// runtime heuristics (pseudocode)
if (!paged_kv_enabled) enable_epilogue_fusion = true;
else if (batch*seq >= 512 || avg_kv_chunk >= 512) enable_epilogue_fusion = true;
else enable_epilogue_fusion = false;
```
Sam: also added a fallback: if kernel flops/time ratio drops below expected -> enqueue unfused path for next requests.
Maria: add telemetry: per-request flag, kernel occupancy, L2_replays, and whether we took fallback. We need a dashboard to correlate model/seq/batch combos.
Junaid: +1. Also track model-arch label (rotary vs sinusoidal rope) so bias/rope fusion only applies when rotary present.
Olga: for rollout: propose canary 5% traffic on dedicated pool with hybrid heuristic, observe 24h, then 25% for another 24h. watch p50/p95/p99, token-cost delta, and error rates.
Sam: ran a quick AB on a synthetic workload that simulates many small KV reads — hybrid wins p99 by ~18% and overall cost regressed <1%.
Perf-bot: bench results uploaded to perf-dashboard: job/2004/qkv-zipper-post-bench, artifacts: nsys.trace, nvprof.out, bench.csv
Maria: great. next steps: 1) add runtime L2-replay counter trigger 2) expose heuristic knobs via config 3) dashboard + canary plan 4) confirm bias/rope gating by model family.
Junaid: one more thought — try lighter-weight epilogue fusion that avoids extra accumulators: keep qkv pack + bias fusion but delay rope into separate thin kernel if regs exceed threshold. Might get most benefits with lower reg pressure.
Sam: good call, I'll prototype 2-level epilogue: full, thin. will post results tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Olga: thanks — flagging on eng-runtime weekly review for visibility.
Sam: thanks team. closing for now, will push branch and canary notes in PR.
